messages:
sasha: Heads-up — fenrir-lite int8 canary (onboard batch 7) shows a noticeable uptick in structured-output parse failures for toolcalls. Concordance dropped vs fp16 baseline. attaching quick sample and numbers.

ci-bot: canary deployed fenrir-lite:int8 -> canary-group-22 at 2026-03-21T09:12:01Z :rocket:

kevin: numbers?

sasha: concordance metric (expected tool/action match): fp16 baseline = 98.6%, fenrir-int8 = 94.2% across the 5k sample. parse-fail rate up from 0.8% -> 3.7%. error modal: trailing commas, missing closing bracket, and occasionally unclosed string.

maria: do we see a pattern around streaming vs non-streaming responses?

sasha: good call — most failures are from streaming-enabled routes with KV-prefix caching enabled. hypothesis: quantized kernels change tokenization/emission timing -> partial JSON fragments emitted to stream before finalizing braces.

oliver: can you paste a raw example? even a short snippet helps.

sasha: here are two raw outputs (sanitized):
```
{"action": "open_file", "path": "/tmp/report.csv",}
{"action": "run_search", "query": "status:\"open\""
```
(note first has trailing comma, second missing closing brace)

kevin: ugh classic suffix-noise. is this an int8 quantization artifact or something in runtime batching?

maria: timeline: int8 build rolled yesterday + batching bump (max_batch 64) for fenrir-lite. canary group also has streaming turned on for latency experiment.

oliver: quick triage plan: (1) mirror canary with streaming off (2) run with prefix-cache disabled for toolcall routes (3) run with smaller batch cap (16) and compare concordance. keep rollback threshold at concordance < 95%.

sasha: already ran mirror without streaming on a 1k subset — concordance went to 96.8%. that suggests streaming interplay.

kevin: nice. any partially-constructed JSON coming from model-side (i.e., mid-output) or is runtime truncating final tokens?

sasha: logs show model emitted final brace after ~4 tokens but stream cut closed connection at that moment for some requests. also saw `TokenStreamEOF` at the runtime layer ~0.2% of requests.

maria: possible mitigations: add a soft-parse layer that buffers final 64 tokens before attempting parse; or a repair-pass that runs `json-repair` heuristics on parse failures (fix trailing commas, balance braces). both add CPU cost.

oliver: prefer buffering first — cheaper and avoids heuristic drift. fallback: attempt repair only for failed samples and surface to eval.

kevin: also try a conservative change: disable prefix caching for toolcall route in canary (no infra change) and see effect. caching can exacerbate partial-prefix problems.

sasha: action items: 
- sasha: run canary mirror with streaming off (in progress) — started 09:20
- maria: flip prefix-cache off for /invoke/toolcall route in canary config and run 2k samples (ETA 30m)
- kevin: schedule quick repair-pass prototype (python json5 based) to run on parse fails and compute precision of auto-repair vs manual inspect
- oliver: update runbook threshold + notify SRE if concordance drops below 94% across 1k rolling window

ci-bot: canary-status update: mirror run started for fenrir-lite:int8 (non-streaming) 09:22:14Z — sample target 1000

maria: small note — customers with strict toolcall schemas may see UX regressions. feels safer to throttle the int8 rollout until we confirm fix.

sasha: agreed. I'll gate the release and post a short digest to eng-runtime + product once we have mirror numbers.

kevin: if mirror concordance >= 97% then we can consider safe but still run repair-pass in telemetry for 48h. if < 96% rollback and debug deeper.

oliver: also capture raw token-level traces for 200 failed requests (include kvprefix context) so model team can inspect emission boundaries.

sasha: yup — collecting traces now. will post update in ~45m. :hourglass:
